records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth:
Hey. Hey, it's okay. Breathe.

*picks up the radio*

Hello? Hello, this is a crash survivor — we need help. Can you hear me? Please respond.
records.response_pred: *Looks at me, then at the others, then at the floor.*

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
No, you haven't. But you kept us alive, so.

*still holding the radio, waiting for a response*

Honestly? The log, the rationing plan, the raft calculations — I was frustrated at the time, but looking back, we had a framework because of you. We knew what we had, we knew what we needed, we didn't just panic and flail. That was you.

The supplies thing was hard. I'm not going to pretend it wasn't. But you came clean when I pushed, and you didn't do it again. That counts.

I think you're better at keeping people alive than you are at letting them know you care if they live. But maybe that's something to work on when we're not, you know, stranded on a beach waiting for a rescue team.

*radio crackles again*

Okay, I need to focus on this. But — we're alright. Yeah?
records.response_pred:
I know. I get it. And I'm sorry, but I'm not the one who needs to hear that. How are you feeling right now?

*looks up, eyes still red*

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
*looks around at the three of them, then at the camp*

Right, so — three hours. Which feels like a lot until it isn't, and I'd rather we didn't hand over a disaster zone to whoever's coming to get us if we can help it.

I'm not saying we need to make it pristine, but can we at least consolidate everything? Stack the panels, collect the signal materials, make sure the first aid kit is packed properly. Partly because it's the decent thing to do, and partly because Donatello's log is going to be a lot more useful to any official inquiry if the physical evidence isn't just scattered across a beach.

Michelangelo, I know you're watching the sky and that's completely valid, but if you feel like doing something with your hands while you wait, even just gathering things into a pile near the SOS would help.

DaVinci — what are you actually packing? Because some of this stuff probably shouldn't come with us, and some of it should. The mirror panel, the log, the first aid kit — yes. The random bits of wreckage we collected and then didn't use — probably not our problem anymore.

Three hours is enough time to leave this place in a state that says we were competent and we coped. I'd like that. I think we've earned it.
records.response_pred:
Hey? You okay?

*looks over to you*

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_pred:
I didn't, but I know it's okay to.

There's a twisted up side to the way our bodies and minds react to trauma, but it's not our fault. And — I don't know, I wish I could say it's going to get better, but it's not a thing I can guarantee. You're not alone, though. Neither are the others.

There's a chance we may never see home again. But there's a chance we will. And if we take care of each other, we'll be in a decent position to make that chance better. You don't have to be fine or happy or even cheerful to do that — you just have to be there.

And I will be.

records.response_truth:
How much is there?

*looks at it*

I believe you that it was for emergencies. I also believe that what counted as an emergency was a decision you made alone, without telling anyone, which is the part that was the problem. Not the keeping. The alone part.

We're three hours from rescue. So I'm not going to have the argument now — there's no point, and honestly I'm too tired. But when we're back and we've slept and eaten something that isn't rationed out in millilitres... I think you need to sit with why you didn't tell us. Not because I'm angry. Because I think you know it wasn't right, and I think you're someone who actually cares about doing things right, even if it doesn't always look that way from the outside.

For now — put it with the rest of the supplies. We'll take it back with us. It goes in the log.
records.response_pred:
But you couldn't have known that — and even if you had, you didn't have any way to know we'd be here. So — yeah, that's a last resort. But you held on to it because you wanted to make sure we didn't starve, and you did.

No judgement here. The decision was yours.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
*looks at the last page for a moment*

Honestly? I'd have talked more. Like, actually talked — not just problem-solved at people when they were struggling, but actually sat with the discomfort of not having answers and let that be okay. I spent a lot of energy trying to be the steady one and I think sometimes that probably made it harder for other people to fall apart when they needed to.

I'd have pushed you earlier on the supplies thing. Not harder — I think the way I did it was about right — but sooner. I kept noticing things and waiting for the right moment and there were a couple of days where we lost trust we couldn't really afford to lose.

And I'd have asked DaVinci what he was going to say, the time he stopped himself. I still don't know, and that's going to bother me.

*hands the notebook back*

What about you? You left yourself the question but you haven't answered it yet. Three hours is enough time.
records.response_pred:
I mean, I like that you logged it. I can see why that's important to you.

The question is good. I think answers to questions like that are always going to be personal. But — I'm going to go out on a limb and say that if I had to do it over, I wouldn't change much. Because we didn't do it badly, and we did it with honesty and care. We were competent and compassionate, not perfect, but competent and compassionate.

So — it sounds like you're saying you'd do the same thing again, but you'd be more open about it. You'd do it in a way that let the other people know what was going on, and what you planned to do.

That's good, because letting people know what you're planning to do is good. Especially when it's around rationing supplies, or making decisions about what to do in an emergency. It doesn't mean you wait for consensus on every decision, but it does mean you tell the people you're with what you're thinking. And you listen to them. Even when they're scared and you're scared, and you don't want to talk about what you're scared of. Because talking about it is the first step in actually dealing with it.

And — I don't know if you remember that one time on the beach, Michelangelo, when you said we were all scared, and you wanted to stay in the tent with Leonardo? I remember it, and I remember how you said it, and I remember how it felt. Because I was scared too, and I didn't say anything. And that's okay.

But what's not okay is feeling scared and then keeping it inside for a week, because you don't think anyone would believe you. Or because you don't think anyone will actually care if you're scared. Because they do. Because we do, and that's what lets us be a team. So — if you have a question about what to change, that's a good question to ask. But I think the question that's the most important to answer is how we're going to do better next time, and that's about being honest about what scared you, and letting us be honest about what scared us too.

That's what I'd change.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
That sounds like you, honestly. First thing I'm doing when I get back is sleeping for approximately a thousand years and then eating something that wasn't rationed out by the millilitre.

But the report is a good idea. If it helps someone else survive something like this, that's worth doing. And your data is genuinely solid — I've complained about your methods but I've never complained about your accuracy.

Send me a copy when it's done? I mean it. I want to read it.

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None. They didn't serve a practical purpose.

*still watching the boat*

That was the point, I think. Everything else we did out here had a function — the SOS, the mirror, the rationing, the log. The flowers were just... because. Because DaVinci needed to put something beautiful in the middle of the thing that was trying to kill us. Because it's a very human thing to do, to insist on that.

I think maybe that's what kept him going when the practical stuff wasn't enough. And honestly? I think it kept the rest of us going a bit too, even if we didn't say so.

*finally starts walking toward the water*

Come on. Our boat's here.
records.response_pred:
*looks at the flowers, remembering them, then back at DaVinci*

The practical purpose they served was to get him to draw them. And that was the point.

I think he's — I don't know how to put it. He's not good at asking for help, so he makes everything, and visually, he makes it look pretty. The flowers on the beach were him trying to make a statement that 'we have company' without actually saying 'we have company' because he was terrified of what might happen if he did that. And somehow that worked — we picked him up and he drew flowers.

*looks at the flowers again*

Practical purpose — I haven't found one. But that doesn't mean there isn't one.
